#6007. How Much Does A GE9X Engine Cost?

While General Electric has not released an official price list for its enormous GE9X engine, it is estimated to cost between $40 million and $45 million, which adds up to $90 million per Boeing 777-9 on paper. This is significantly more than the retail prices of super-sized widebody powerplants like the GE90 and the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB.

However, commanding the highest commercial engine price in aviation history has not resulted in simple assembly-line profits. Early factory batches cost significantly more to build than launch airline contracts pay back while Boeing finishes testing the airframe. In fact, GE executives warned in January that initial production losses on the GE9X would double this year as shipments increased ahead of commercial service.

Behind that exorbitant price tag lies an unrivaled sole-source agreement on Boeing's flagship twinjet, backed by heat-resistant ceramics, 3D-printed alloys, and record-breaking thrust. However, after volume discounts and multi-year maintenance contracts are factored in, airlines rarely pay anywhere near catalog value. With years of mechanical issues, grounded test aircraft, and mid-turbine seal repairs, this engineering accomplishment has become a high-stakes financial race to 2027.

General Electric secured its sole-source grip on the Boeing 777X through a calculated competitive truce years earlier. Back in 2008, GE refused to power the Airbus A350-1000 so it would not undercut its lucrative GE90 franchise on the Boeing 777-300ER. When Boeing later launched the 777X, Pratt & Whitney and Rolls-Royce stayed away after GE Aviation head David Joyce flatly rejected sharing the airframe.

Without a rival engine maker bidding prices down, GE unveiled the GE9X at the 2013 Dubai Air Show alongside massive launch commitments. Emirates agreed to buy 300 engines in a paper deal valued at over $11 billion, roughly $37 million apiece before discounts, while Qatar Airways followed with a $3.8 billion order covering 50 jets. However, if carriers negotiate significant volume discounts, actual airline invoices hardly resemble flashy airshow figures.

GE frequently incorporates engine hardware into multi-year service contracts in order to further obfuscate per-unit pricing. For instance, because it included a 12-year TrueChoice overhaul agreement, Singapore Airlines' 2022 order for 22 spare GE9X engines had a $2.8 billion headline value, well over $100 million per engine. With this 'razor-and-blades' strategy, GE is able to absorb early production losses while securing three decades of revenue from sole-source repairs on demanding ultra-long-haul routes.

Raw mechanical muscle anchors the GE9X's lofty sticker price, proven during a November 2017 ground run in Peebles, Ohio, when a test engine hit 134,300 pounds of thrust (597 kN) to claim a Guinness World Record. After the historic test, Joyce said: "While we didn't set out to break the thrust Guinness World Records title, we are proud of the engine's performance, which is a testament to our talented employees and partners who design and build outstanding products for our customers."

Airline pilots will never use that record power on a routine departure. That's because General Electric purposefully derated the production turbofan below the 115,300 pounds of thrust (513 kN) of its earlier GE90-115B brother. With the help of a front fan bigger than a Boeing 737-800 cabin and 16 steel-tipped carbon-fiber blades that reduce fuel consumption by 10%, the operating cooler prolongs the time between shop overhauls, maintains costly core blades, and saves fuel over thousands of flights.

Size and efficiency anchored GE's sales pitch to global long-haul carriers when US regulators cleared the engine in September 2020. According to Composites World, GE Aviation CEO John Slattery declared at certification: "There is no substitute that can achieve the combination of size, power and fuel efficiency." Test flights aboard GE's Boeing 747-400 flying testbed even ran so quietly that a pilot checked cockpit gauges just to confirm the engine was still running.

A closer look at the edge that Boeing's iconic 747 still holds over the gargantuan Airbus A380 to this day.

The engine's core is made of exotic, heat-resistant materials, which contribute significantly to its price tag of over $40 million. Ceramic matrix composites, lightweight, space-age ceramics that can resist temperatures up to 2,400°F (1,315°C) without melting, are packed into the GE9X's combustor and turbine. This allows the engine to run hotter and more effectively while requiring far less cooling air. Program leader Ted Ingling stated: "The ceramics allowed us to go to 60:1 [pressure ratio] inside the GE9X. So if I'm Boeing and I'm looking for the lightest-weight engine so that I can turn that weight into passengers - it's range, it's fuel, it's passengers."

Industrial 3D printing increases costs by generating over 300 complicated pieces per engine, such as one-piece fuel nozzles that reduce weight by 25% and electron-beam-melted titanium-aluminum turbine blades. Even with unusual alloys, engineers strove to make layouts tidy enough for line mechanics. In November 2025, GE Aerospace technology chief Mohamed Ali stated: "There is elegance in simplicity with the fewest number of parts. If the architecture is done correctly, you'll occasionally have to fix a sink or replace appliances, but the house functions and is practical."

The surging cost of keeping caro jets airworthy in the era of e-commerce.

The GE9X has had a difficult development process, characterized by frequent technical setbacks that have repeatedly delayed Boeing's certification deadline, despite its exorbitant valuation. The 777-9's first flight was postponed until engineers completed a permanent redesign in 2019 due to early compressor vane wear, which required General Electric to airlift four engines back to its facilities by Antonov freighters.

Long after the engine was certified by US regulators in September 2020, new mechanical curveballs caused turbulence during flight testing. All four 777-9 prototypes were grounded for five months after a titanium thrust link broke on a test plane returning from Hawaii in late 2022. In January 2026, shop inspectors found a damaged mid-turbine seal that was prematurely wearing due to excessive heat stress.

Although US regulators made approval of the patch a severe requirement for final 777-9 certification, GE rebuilt the seal and started shipping improved engines to Boeing in the third quarter. Overwater ETOPS testing was halted by that congestion, which also prevented GE from recording shipment income. That left the company scrambling to prove the repair will not derail its 2027 service-entry target.

How the 767 is bridging the gap to a new generation of widebody twinjets in its twilight.

Before a single paying passenger boards the aircraft, seven years of schedule setbacks had cost both manufacturers billions of dollars. After delaying the first 777-9 deliveries to 2027, Boeing incurred approximately $15 billion in cumulative pre-tax program expenditures through late 2025. In the meantime, General Electric warned investors in January that early plant losses would double this year as production capacity increases. The company spent more than $2 billion creating the GE9X.

Billions were paid by irate buyers to make up for lost widebodies. Emirates President Sir Tim Clark blasted Boeing in October 2024 to Business Insider: "I fail to see how Boeing can make any meaningful forecasts of delivery dates. Emirates has had to make significant and highly expensive amendments to our fleet programs as a result of Boeing's multiple contractual shortfalls." Dubai responded by committing $5 billion to overhaul Airbus A380-800 and 777-300ER cabins, while Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr stripped the 777-9 from summer 2027 schedules and kept aging Airbus A340-300 quadjets flying longer.

When the delayed twinjet finally reaches airport gates, travelers will step into a noticeably calmer cabin shaped by its composite wing and quieter engines. Boeing sculpted thinner sidewalls to widen the interior to 235 inches (597 cm) for 18-inch (45.7 cm) economy seats, paired with larger windows and higher cabin humidity. Cruise pressurization drops to 6,000 feet (1,829 meters), helping long-haul fliers land feeling far fresher.

The GE9X may be the largest turbofan ever built, but by just how much does it surpass its mighty predecessor, the GE90?

Everything now hinges on a single component: the redesigned GE9X mid-turbine seal. Until federal regulators sign off on the modification, Boeing cannot secure final type certification to clear the 777-9 for commercial service, keeping 2027 delivery milestones razor-tight across 682 firm orders and more than 1,360 installed engines.

At the same time, a serious financial stalemate looms over roughly two dozen already-built 777-9 jets parked outside Seattle awaiting approval. Emirates officially rejected its first batch of 10 parked airframes in July. Emirates president Tim Clark dismissed them as "baked bean cans," and Lufthansa has likewise balked at taking older aircraft that require extensive retrofits. As a result, Boeing and General Electric must either absorb costly rework or hunt for new buyers.

Looking ahead to 2030, Airbus is evaluating a stretched 400-seat A350-2000 that may require greater thrust than Rolls-Royce's Trent XWB-97 can deliver. If Airbus launches that larger twinjet, industry watchers will track whether GE breaks its 2008 truce and ends Rolls-Royce's exclusive grip on the A350 family, potentially putting the $40 million GE9X, or a tailored derivative, beneath an Airbus wing.

#6006. British Airways Visa Card Review: Is It Worth The $95 Annual Fee?

The British Airways Visa Signature® Card is one of Chase’s co-branded airline credit cards, and British Airways Club is certainly a popular frequent flyer program, given the overall value of the Avios ecosystem, plus the number of destinations in the United States that British Airways serves.

Who should be applying for the British Airways Visa, and under what circumstances is it worth spending money on it? Let’s take a look at what you need to know about this card, and what the best alternatives are.

Link: Learn more about the British Airways Visa Signature® Card

Before jumping into a closer look at every aspect of the British Airways Visa Card, here’s a high-level view of the card’s key features, perks, and fees:

Here are my thoughts on the biggest British Airways Visa Card pros and cons:

If you’re considering the British Airways Visa Signature Card, its welcome bonus, application rules, and annual fee are all probably top of mind. So let’s start by taking a look at these important details.

The British Airways Visa currently offers the following welcome bonus: Earn 75,000 Avios after you spend $5,000 on purchases within the first three months of account opening.

Based on my current points and miles valuations, which put Avios at 1.2 cents apiece, this current bonus is worth about $900. That’s a pretty solid welcome bonus, especially for a card with a moderate annual fee.

The British Airways Visa has a $95 annual fee. This is not waived for the first year, and there’s no additional fee to add authorized users.

British Airways’ credit card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s potentially a great card to use for purchases abroad.

The welcome bonus on the British Airways Visa isn’t available to those who currently have the card, or those who have received a new cardmember bonus on the card in the past 24 months. You are eligible for this card if you’ve had the Iberia Visa Signature® Card and/or Aer Lingus Visa Signature® Card, despite the similarities between the cards.

Chase’s other general policies on card approvals apply as well, including the 5/24, whereby you generally won’t be approved for a Chase card if you’ve opened five or more credit cards in the last 24 months.

The British Airways Visa Card has no foreign transaction fees, but does the rewards structure warrant putting spending on the card? It might, but only thanks to additional bonuses offered by the card, which incentivize spending.

The British Airways Visa doesn’t have terribly exciting bonus categories. You earn:

There are lots of great credit cards for airfare purchases and hotel purchases. This isn’t a card I would be putting much spending on unless you’re trying to earn a Travel Together Ticket, in which case it could definitely be worth it. More on that below.

British Airways Club is a transfer partner of Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, so it could make sense to put spending on a card earning one of those currencies if you want to earn Avios at an accelerated rate.

There are lots of great uses of British Airways Avios. British Airways Club has roughly distance based award pricing, and the program offers value in situations where other programs might not. Generally speaking, here’s where I see value with Avios:

British Airways is known for adding large taxes and surcharges to some of its own award flights, so this is worth keeping in mind.

Personally I find Avios to be one of the most useful frequent flyer programs for redeeming points, thanks to the number of redemptions this opens up.

Often one of the big challenges people have with points is figuring out how to pool them since you typically need enough points in a single account for a redemption. A cool feature of the British Airways Club program is that you can form household accounts. This allows you to pool the Avios you earn with up to six other people registered at the same address as you.

This is especially awesome in the context of a credit card welcome bonus, since you can pool a ton of Avios in a single account if you have two people get the card in a household, etc.

There are some benefits to the British Airways Visa Card that could alone justify having this card. For some people, it will be worth spending money on the card to unlock some perks, while for others just having the card and not spending money on it offers sufficient benefits. Let’s look at what those benefits are, and how they work.

One of the best benefits of the British Airways Signature Visa is that it offers a 10% discount on British Airways flights starting in the United States. To take advantage of this, just book through ba.com/chase10, and use your card to pay while using promotion code BACHASE10.

If you fly British Airways with any frequency, this could cover the annual fee over and over. See this post for everything you need to know about the British Airways Visa flight discount.

If you have the British Airways Visa Card and redeem Avios for a reward flight, you can receive up to $600 in statement credits annually. You can earn up to three statement credits, as follows:

There are some basic terms to be aware of:

British Airways now also offers Reward Flight Saver from the United States, allowing you to redeem more Avios and pay lower surcharges. Getting a further statement credit of up to $200 on that is pretty great.

One of the potentially great perks of the British Airways Visa is that you can earn a Travel Together Ticket when you spend $30,000 on the card in a calendar year.

This companion ticket will be deposited in your British Airways Club account four to six weeks after you’ve completed the required spending.

With this certificate, you can book a British Airways award ticket at the full cost of Avios (plus taxes, fees, and surcharges), and then for the second passenger you don’t have to pay any Avios, but rather just have to pay all the fees.

This also offers a lot of flexibility — you can also use the voucher as a solo traveler and get 50% off the Avios required for a ticket. Your ticket can originate anywhere in the world, and you can even travel on Aer Lingus or Iberia.

This can represent a fantastic deal for first and business class travel, given how much those tickets would otherwise cost. This isn’t for everyone, though it has the potential to represent a good value, and I know it’s a feature that many value.

See this post for everything you need to know about the British Airways Visa companion voucher.

As a Visa Signature card, the British Airways Visa comes with the following shopping and travel protection benefits:

You’ll want to review the card’s benefits guide for any exclusions and rules that apply.

The British Airways Visa Card has a solid welcome bonus, and that could be a legitimate motivator for picking up this card. However, personally this isn’t a card I would use for everyday spending, since you can earn British Airways Avios at a better rate with other American Express or Chase cards. It also lacks a few benefits that many other airline credit cards offer, including a free checked bag and priority boarding.

That said, I absolutely think this card is worth holding onto if you fly British Airways with any frequency because:

There are several Avios currencies, with three belonging to International Airlines Group (IAG) airlines — there’s British Airways, Aer Lingus, and Iberia. There are also two other US-based credit cards that directly earn Avios from these airlines. Specifically, we’re talking about the Iberia Visa Card (learn more) and Aer Lingus Visa Card (learn more).

Which of these cards should you select? They have a lot in common:

The differences mainly come in the form of the perks associated with just holding onto the cards, and also the perks associated with spending $30,000 on the cards in a calendar year:

The best card to select comes down to which benefits you value most. Also, remember that you’re eligible for all three of these cards, should you be interested, so you don’t necessarily have to choose between them.

See here for a full comparison of cards earning Avios.

If you want to earn British Airways Avios, I’d recommend getting a card that earns either Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, or Chase Ultimate Rewards points. Here’s why:

With that in mind, which cards should you consider? Here are some of my favorite Chase Ultimate Rewards-earning cards:

If you’re over 5/24 or simply prefer Amex points or Capital One miles, here are some top choices:

The British Airways Visa is one of the best co-branded airline credit cards out there, in my opinion. The card offers a solid welcome bonus, and it can be worth spending money on the card to earn a companion ticket.

Beyond that, the card can be worth having for the discounts offered on both paid tickets (up to 10% off) or award tickets (up to $200 in statement credits), which can cover the annual fee over and over. That said, the card would be even stronger if it offered a free checked bag and lounge access as benefits — though I’d expect the annual to increase if those were added, especially the latter perk.

When it comes to earning British Airways Avios long term, personally I’d much rather earn Amex, Bilt, Capital One, and Chase points, and transfer them to British Airways. Not only does this allow you to earn points at a much faster rate, but it also gives you a lot more flexibility.

#6005. Sweeping permitting overhaul passes Senate, on to House

From left, Sens. Mike Lee, R-Utah., Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., and Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., hold a news conference on the measure in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

The Senate passed a bill Thursday evening that would overhaul the federal permitting system for electric power lines, power lines wind and solar farms, hard rock mining and oil drilling projects and more.

It's the culmination of a yearslong effort intended to address industry concerns that it is too difficult to build any major infrastructure project in the United States. Supporters overcame opposition from more than half the Democratic Caucus, which will be a factor when the bill moves to the House after the Thanksgiving recess.

The bill passed on a 62-33 vote, with 31 Democrats joining two Republicans, Josh Hawley of Missouri and Mike Rounds of South Dakota, in opposition.

Shortly after the post-cloture time expired late Thursday, the Senate voted on passage of the legislation, including a substitute amendment consisting of revised text of the original permitting bill that the bipartisan authors unveiled before the midterm elections.

However, the chamber did not consider any additional amendments to the bill, as initially planned by the sponsors, including Environment and Public Works Chairman Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., panel ranking member Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., Energy and Natural Resources Chairman Mike Lee, R-Utah, and panel ranking member Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

The bill includes changes to how reviews are conducted and permits are issued under the National Environmental Policy Act, National Historic Preservation Act, Endangered Species Act, Federal Power Act and Clean Water Act.

It includes provisions intended to ensure electricity ratepayers are not saddled with the costs of bringing power to data centers, and would give the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission new authority over interstate transmission lines.

It also would provide legal recourse when administrations discriminate against certain forms of energy or seek to revisit permits on ideological grounds. That's intended in part to address the Trump administration’s actions to delay or block solar and wind energy projects.

Democrats walked away from negotiations last year due to Trump administration actions to block offshore wind construction. However they ultimately said they received sufficient assurances that the administration would let stalled wind and solar projects move forward.

The "big four" senators on the permitting bill solicited feedback and changes sought by various lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, and were open to votes on additional amendments — so long as they didn't undo the measure's core tenets.

"This bill has threaded a needle the likes of which this chamber has not seen in a while, and we’ve got to take advantage of this opportunity," Capito said before passage.

Ultimately, Oregon Democratic Sens. Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden would not consent to a time agreement allowing consideration of a finite number of amendments because Republicans wouldn't allow up-or-down votes at a simple-majority threshold on some of theirs. Merkley then objected to a unanimous consent request to consider amendments on the floor.

Wyden was pushing for a vote on an amendment that would prohibit construction of data centers on federal public lands. Merkley was pushing for amendments that included barring data centers from benefiting from “project certainty” protections against future presidents revoking their permits, and limiting presidential power to impose tariffs on clean energy project components, like wind turbines.

The Senate had already adopted the substitute amendment introduced by the bill’s sponsors during a procedural vote on Wednesday. But the lack of a unanimous consent agreement to take up more amendments meant that an additional manager's package of changes to the substitute fell by the wayside.

That amendment would have narrowed the instances where exemptions from National Historic Preservation Act reviews would be allowed, increased the annual authorization for the Historic Preservation Fund by 50 percent, and addressed concerns about the use of eminent domain when permitting transmission projects raised by Hawley and Rounds.

The sponsors introduced an updated version of their manager’s amendment Thursday afternoon that would refine exemptions from the ratepayer projection provisions so that artificial intelligence "hyperscalers" can't escape through a loophole.

The original manager's amendment sought to exempt internet and telecommunications providers' facilities, but the language was broad enough that cloud storage and other "information services" exclusions could potentially benefit data centers.

None of those changes made it into the bill as a result of the stalemate over amendments, and Merkley objected on the floor to incorporating just the manager's package.

The bill has been endorsed by a wide range of industry groups, who argue that the current federal permitting regime makes it too difficult to finance, plan and construct projects domestically. This includes the American Petroleum Institute, the American Clean Power Association, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the National Association of Manufacturers.

The White House expressed its support for the bill in a statement of administration policy this month.

The bill now moves on to the House, where it seemingly has the votes to pass.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said last week that the bill can pass in that chamber, while a number of Democrats including the centrist Blue Dog Coalition and Reps. Scott Peters, D-Calif., co-chair of the bipartisan Climate Solutions Caucus, and Nikki Budzinski, D-Ill., have expressed support.

Budzinski was elected chair of the 112-member New Democrat Coalition last week for the next Congress, and that group issued a statement speaking favorably of permitting while stopping short of endorsing the bill as currently drafted.

However, attendance on the House GOP side after Thanksgiving could be an issue: more than 30 lawmakers regularly skipped votes this week, the majority of them Republicans.

And many Democrats have called on Heinrich and Whitehouse to punt consideration of the bill to the new Congress, when their party will have large majorities in both chambers.

Merkley, who is in line to chair the Environment and Public Works Committee, and House Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman, D-Calif. — the expected chairman of that panel — both said the bill included too many provisions Democrats opposed in order to garner Republican support.

Some of the nation’s largest environmental groups including the Sierra Club and Natural Resources Defense Council oppose the bill. A coalition of 17 Democratic states also expressed their opposition. And some Native American tribes and organizations, including the National Congress of American Indians, also expressed their opposition.

"I’m hoping to have a full opportunity to address the many legitimate concerns that stakeholders have raised with this bill," Merkley said before the vote Thursday night.

But Heinrich and Whitehouse resisted calls to delay the bill, arguing that President Donald Trump is in office for two more years and that any bill needs his support to be signed into law. They added that they will be able to address environmental issues under their majority, and that this bill would represent the “floor” of their ambitions.

While Republicans have called for changes to the federal permitting system for decades, the effort gained steam with Democrats after the passage of their 2022 reconciliation law, which they dubbed the Inflation Reduction Act, or IRA.

As part of the deal to get then-Senate Energy and Natural Resources Chairman Joe Manchin III, D-W.Va., on board with the IRA, the Biden administration agreed to support a bill overhauling the federal permitting system. Manchin introduced a bill that included changes to NEPA and transmission permitting, and would approve all remaining permits needed for the Mountain Valley Pipeline in his home state.

However, his effort ultimately fell short on a 47-47 procedural vote to attach the bill to that year’s defense authorization measure.

In the 118th Congress Manchin tried again, and in 2024 he and then-Energy and Natural Resources ranking member John Barrasso, R-Wyo., introduced what Manchin called a “perfectly crafted balance.” The committee approved that bill in July 2024, but it was never voted on by the full Senate.

Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich made a collective commitment to address permitting overhaul when they stepped into their current roles in January 2025, and spent nearly 21 months working on the legislation.

Since Manchin’s first bill, the political calculus changed.

After decades of stagnant energy demand, electricity prices began rising in part due to the expansion of data centers. Consumers also became increasingly frustrated with their local utilities over affordability concerns, which in turn spurred more lawmakers across the country, including on Capitol Hill, to critically examine their practices.

Lee also pushed for language streamlining NHPA reviews, which had not been a focus of earlier permitting discussion. He's argued that the law has expanded beyond its originally intended scope and become a major barrier to infrastructure projects in Western states like Utah.

#6004. Norse Atlantic Collapses: Airline Cancels Flights, Strands Passengers

Back in August 2026, all-Boeing 787 airline Norse Atlantic Airways announced it was in a rough financial spot, and was pursuing a sale, merger, or other arrangement. Not a whole lot of progress was made in subsequent months, and just this morning, the airline announced that it was in a “critical” financial situation.

Well, it seems that it didn’t take long for things to get much worse, as the airline has seemingly canceled all flights just hours later, leaving travelers stranded.

Earlier today, Norse Atlantic provided an update on its financial situation and ongoing strategic review. There’s no point in paraphrasing this, so here’s the direct statement from the airline:

The Company’s financial situation is critical. It is dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations. Norse, supported by its advisors, has explored various strategic alternatives and entertains discussions for a potential takeover. In parallel, the Board and management have diligently considered other available options, including ACMI contracts. Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution.

To state the obvious, this sounded really, really bad. When the company was publicly stating that its “financial situation is critical” and that it needed to secure financing to meet “short-term liquidity needs,” you knew things weren’t good. I expected we’d see something bad happen in the coming weeks, but it didn’t take that long.

Norse Atlantic has canceled its own scheduled flights effective immediately. On top of that, the airline was leasing two jets to Pakistan International Airlines, and those flights were also canceled with very little notice, “due to an unexpected operational suspension” by Norse Atlantic. Travelers were literally checking in at the airport when they realized the airline was grounded.

Due to an unexpected operational suspension by our wet-lease partner Norse Air without prior notice, tonight’s PK786 (London–Islamabad) & PK710 (Manchester–Lahore) are cancelled.We deeply regret the disruption. Efforts have been made to mitigate the impact, and from tomorrow,…

So while the company hasn’t formally announced that it’s liquidating, it’s clear that operations are at least suspended, and we’ll see how this all plays out.

The airline industry can be a funny business, and there’s no clearer example of that than Norse Atlantic Airways. The airline launched in 2022, with the goal of operating long haul, low cost flights, particularly across the Atlantic.

That wasn’t exactly a unique business model, because this was exactly what Norwegian did, before it discontinued long haul flights in 2021. Not only was the idea sort of copied, but Norse Atlantic had some executives from Norwegian, and even picked up the planes that Norwegian previously flew.

But as is all too common in the airline industry, clearly they thought it would be different this time around… it wasn’t. So in 2024 we saw the airline update its business model, making the focus less about operating regularly scheduled commercial flights, and more about leasing out aircraft, all while reducing its fleet.

The company got a lifeline when IndiGo decided to lease some Norse Atlantic 787s to dabble in long haul flying, ahead of the airline taking delivery of its own Airbus A350s. However, between all the airspace closures, high oil costs, and generally declining performance at IndiGo as the airline increasingly moved away from its core strengths, the airline recently decided to scrap that experiment, and stop leasing planes from Norse Atlantic.

Since then, opportunities for Norse Atlantic have been limited. The airline did manage to lease a couple of Dreamliners to the “new” Pakistan International Airlines, but for an airline with 12 planes, that hardly pays the bills.

Norse Atlantic did still operate some of its own flights, but in a very limited capacity. The airline had some flights from Europe to Thailand, South Africa, and the United States, but most were seasonal, and they were a fraction of what they previously were. Clearly they just didn’t have enough money to “keep the lights on” anymore.

I am curious to see what comes next for Norse Atlantic’s 787s. The airline doesn’t own them, but instead, they’ll presumably return to their leasing companies. I can’t help but point out that Southwest Airlines wants to start long haul flights. The airline had been considering a Boeing 787 order, and was possibly even looking at ways to get planes faster than from a direct order (which requires waiting for years).

Could these dozen Norse Atlantic 787s somehow end up at Southwest? The interiors would just need some updates (assuming the airline wants to offer business class), but talk about a quick way to grow a decent sized fleet.

This morning, Norse Atlantic released a statement admitting that its “financial situation is critical,” and that the company’s future is “dependent on securing financing to meet short-term liquidity needs.” That wasn’t exactly a great sign, but little did we know that the company would collapse just hours later, as the airline has now ceased all flying, including on a wet lease basis.

Financial issues at the company started when… well, it launched. Norse Atlantic was just a direct replica of Norwegian, which had failed. When the airline realized that the long haul, low cost business model doesn’t really work, they tried to pivot to wet leasing. And while there’s some demand for that, it’s also not a 100% consistent business in terms of demand.

I feel horribly for all the frontline employees at Norse Atlantic who put their best foot forward. May they find good opportunities at other airlines.

What do you make of Norse Atlantic’s seeming collapse?

There's no doubt about it: The airport lounge wars are heating up with credit card issuers like American Express, Capital One and Chase launching new outposts at a blistering pace.

American Express maintains the largest footprint with its Global Lounge Collection, while Capital One has been expanding its map of Capital One airport lounges.

However, it's Chase in particular that has turned up the heat, expanding its U.S. lounge collection since 2023, with more on the way, including a location at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

Here’s everything you need to know about the family of Chase Sapphire Lounges by The Club, their amenities and how to access them.

Apply for the : Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening (see ).

Chase’s lounge collection includes nine Sapphire Lounge locations. The JFK location is temporarily closed.

Additional lounges are planned at the following airports:

Chase has partnered with Airport Dimensions to build out its lounges. Airport Dimensions currently operates dozens of lounges worldwide, most of which are branded as “The Club” or “Club Aspire” and are largely accessible via Priority Pass membership.

Related: Is a Priority Pass lounge membership actually worth it?

This location was the first branded Chase lounge to open in the U.S.

It's located in the Terminal B-to-C connector near gates B39 and B40 and is accessible post-security from Terminals B, C and E. Passengers departing from Terminal A will need to clear security again when returning to their departure terminal.

The lounge has an expansive footprint, at over 11,000 square feet with seating for over 200 guests, though lines to get in can certainly form at busy times, with waits topping an hour. It is open from 5 a.m. until 11 p.m. daily.

In addition to a variety of restaurant- and living room-style seating areas, there is a self-serve buffet at one end. Guests can also order a la carte dishes created by Boston-area chef Douglass Williams as well as specialty cocktails and Massachusetts-brewed beers from table-mounted QR codes.

The lounge also has wellness rooms with massage chairs and comfortable loungers for relaxation and products from Brooklyn-based fragrance brand Apotheke.

The newest Chase Sapphire Lounge opened at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in July 2026. Located post-security near gate D25 in Terminal D, the 18,000-square-foot lounge is one of the largest in the Sapphire network. It is open from 5 a.m. until 10 p.m. daily.

In addition to Chase's signature made-to-order dining (with dishes like blue corn butterscotch pancakes from favorite local restaurant Encina), an all-day buffet and full-service bar, the DFW location introduces several features unique to the network. Travelers can visit the first dedicated Sapphire whiskey lounge featuring guided tastings of Texas whiskeys (and a specialty honey pecan Old Fashioned cocktail), book a complimentary 30-minute Face Haus treatment, freshen up in a shower suite or relax in dedicated rest areas.

Families will also appreciate the children's play area and private nursing room, while travelers in a hurry can take advantage of a grab-and-go food station — a feature Chase is currently testing at this location.

Chase and Airport Dimensions revamped The Etihad Lounge at Dulles, located in Concourse A near gate A14.

The space is small, at just over 5,000 square feet, but features two levels with various seating areas, including a library-themed space, gender-neutral restrooms, shower suites, a reflection room for quiet meditation and a family room.

As with the other lounge locations, this one features locally-inspired food and cocktails plus locally-brewed java from Commonwealth Joe Coffee Roasters.

The lounge is currently open from 6 a.m. until 10 p.m. daily.

Chase's lounge at LAS is located past security in Terminal 1, Concourse C, between gates 23 and 24. It opened in December 2025, spans two stories, covers 4,590 square feet and has seating for up to 87 people. It is open from 4:30 a.m. until 11 p.m. daily.

Though compact compared to the other Chase Sapphire lounges, this one packs a punch in terms of ambience. The space features colorful artwork and a lively atmosphere, not to mention a rather glamorous "Champagne parlor" plus a menu of cocktails inspired by Sin City and a wine list curated by New York retailer Parcelle.

Food options include bites like pork buns and a spicy cucumber salad from Momofuku.

There are no showers, spa services or meditation rooms here, though.

The issuer is bringing a lounge to LAX on an unconfirmed date. It will be adjacent to gate 148 near the connector to the west gates at Tom Bradley International Terminal.

Now that all terminals at LAX are connected airside (post-security), any traveler with access could theoretically visit this lounge, although it is a bit of a hike from other terminals.

The new lounge will measure around 9,000 square feet, which is on the smaller side — especially for an airport the size of LAX — so expect some long wait times once it opens, much as you'll find at the nearby Centurion Lounge.

The Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club at JFK is located in Terminal 4 near gate A2, not far from the security checkpoint and up one level.

Like the location at IAD, this space is a redesigned Etihad Lounge rather than one Chase created from scratch, and it's rather limited in size at just 7,600 square feet.

It is usually open from 4:30 a.m. until 9 p.m. daily, but at the time of publication, it is temporarily closed due to plumbing issues. There are grab-and-go food options, though.

Typically, you can find a buffet of small plates, plus seasonal items (but always the famous burger) available for order via QR code. This lounge also has three shower suites.

The LaGuardia Sapphire Lounge is the largest of the collection, at 21,000 square feet spanning two floors. It is located in Terminal B and is open from 4:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. daily.

The lounge houses plenty of spacious seating areas, including a restaurant-style section and more casual vignettes. There are also family-oriented areas, including a children's playroom and arcade.

The lounge offers a buffet and a seasonal menu featuring select dishes from Sailor, a restaurant in Fort Greene, Brooklyn, plus locally inspired cocktails by Apotheke and wines chosen by Parcelle.

There's also a wellness area where guests can enjoy Face Haus facial treatments, guided meditations from podcaster Devi Brown and private rest pods.

Uniquely, the lounge features Reserve Suites, Chase’s lounge-within-a-lounge concept, which you can reserve for $2,200-$3,000 for a three-hour private retreat.

This 20,000-square-foot Chase lounge opened in February 2025 in the connector between Terminal D (home of Air Canada, Delta Air Lines, Spirit Airlines, Alaska Airlines and United Airlines) and Terminal E (where gates for Frontier Airlines, JetBlue, Alaska Airlines, Southwest Airlines and Spirit Airlines can be found).

If you go through the Terminal D Transportation Security Administration checkpoint, it is upstairs and is open from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.

It offers a similar layout to other Chase lounges, but with some unique features including a wellness center with two treatment rooms for facials, two shower suites, a game room, Elixr Coffee drinks and a bar with Philadelphia Eagles-themed cocktails, plus a beer garden and local dishes courtesy of Fishtown eatery Middle Child Clubhouse.

The Sapphire Lounge at PHX opened in November 2024 and is located at the new eight-gate facility in Terminal 4 near gate D11.

This lounge began accepting reservations in June 2025. Sapphire Reserve cardmembers departing from Phoenix can reserve their visit from 14 days up to 24 hours before arriving at the lounge, so you don't have to be physically present to make your reservation. That's because this is the smallest lounge, at just 3,500 square feet.

The lounge is open from 4:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. daily, though its site notes that hours may vary.

There are a few different seating areas, with the tables around the central cocktail bar being in high demand. There's also an indoor terrace separated from the terminal, where a retrofitted Airstream food truck serves specialties from Gallo Blanco. Guests will also find Arizona-based Press Coffee drinks on hand, craft cocktails and a Parcelle-selected list of wines.

Located in San Diego's Terminal 2, this 11,000-square-foot Chase lounge opened in December 2024 with plenty of surfer-themed art and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the tarmac.

The lounge is open from 5 a.m. until 10 p.m. daily and has a swanky wraparound cocktail bar, a small buffet area (plus à la carte dishes by Oscars Mexican Seafood on offer via QR code) and plenty of distinct seating areas.

There's also a wellness area with four relaxation pods and Face Haus treatments, a family room, showers and a nursing room.

Chase is planning a new 16,000-square-foot Sapphire Lounge in Concourse A at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The Port of Seattle approved the project in October 2026, with a planned $70 million investment covering the initial build-out and a future refurbishment. An opening date has not yet been announced.

Related: 5 ways to ensure you have lounge access before your next flight

Those with the (see rates and fees), (see rates and fees), J.P. Morgan Reserve or Ritz-Carlton™ Credit Card can access these lounges.

The information for the J.P. Morgan Reserve card and the Ritz-Carlton Credit Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Cardholders can access the lounges up to three hours before departure (or up to five hours before a connecting flight) and can also bring up to two guests per visit for free. If you're a cardholder and wish to bring more than two guests, you'll be charged a fee. Children under 2 can enter for free.

Related: Chase Sapphire Reserve review: A premium card for power travelers

While Priority Pass members previously got to access a Chase Lounge once per calendar year, this benefit has been discontinued.

Select Etihad travelers (the airline’s Gold and Platinum elite members and those flying in business or first class on Etihad-operated flights) can visit the IAD and JFK locations before their flights.

Related: A guide to guest policies for airport lounges

For years, Amex's network of Centurion Lounges was the major player in the card-run lounge space, but in recent years, Chase has quickly caught up, opening a series of lounges around the country in record time, with more on the way. With the airport lounge competition intensifying among major credit card issuers, the real winners are cardholders, though.

That said, these lounges feel like they're getting more crowded by the day, so when you get to an airport with one, make a beeline to the entrance and put your name on the list for access just in case there's a wait. After all, you wouldn't want to miss out on their many amenities.

#6001. Departing Senate spending kingpins angle for last earmark hurrah

Sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, left, and Mitch McConnell , R-Ky., won't be smiling as much if Democrats force a punt on spending bills to next year. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo)

Newly released Senate appropriations bills would distribute $8.7 billion in "congressionally directed spending" secured by 78 senators for their home states — earmarked dollars that could disappear if Congress resorts to a stopgap funding measure to avert a partial government shutdown after Dec. 11.

Nearly 4,000 individual earmarks are contained in nine of the 12 draft fiscal 2027 spending bills, a CQ Roll Call tally found; the remaining three bills — Defense, State-Foreign Operations and Legislative Branch — don't have any.

There's typically some overlap between House and Senate projects that would get weeded out in final negotiations to avoid duplication. But for comparison's sake, House Republicans included nearly 6,700 line items worth $8.2 billion in their earmarked spending bills.

Democrats have signaled they'll push for a continuing resolution into the first quarter of next year enabling them to rewrite the full-year fiscal 2027 bills when they take the gavels in January, possibly upping the overall pot of earmarked funds — or at least divvying up the pie more favorably to blue states and districts.

But that would mean the final attempt by departing lawmakers like Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, and longtime Senate GOP leader and senior appropriator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, to deliver for their states might be all for naught.

And top Democrats with substantial earmarking success under GOP governance, such as Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., will have to start from scratch.

Here are some key stats on senators' earmarks in the latest batch of spending bills Collins is trying to get across the finish line.

Naturally, much of the spoils go to Senate Appropriations Committee members, and that's no different this year. But with so many more Democrats requesting projects — often jointly with their fellow delegation member — individual contributions may appear diluted given they have to share the credit.

That dilution shows up in the rankings when allocating credit in a way that avoids double-counting — everyone gets an equal share of his or her joint projects, so $20 million sponsored jointly by two senators will appear as $10 million for each. Solo earmarkers in this scenario face no such dilution.

Using the even-split methodology, the top 10 — all senior appropriators — look like this:

Another way to look at it is by simply adding up every instance of a senator affixing his or her name to a project, which leads to double-counting but gives them full credit for every earmark secured, even with jointly requested projects.

Finally, there's the solo earmarker leaderboard, only counting dollars secured without any co-sponsors:

McConnell and Collins hit the trifecta, ending up among the top three in all three scenarios.

Related: Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

Unlike the House, where states with the largest populations receive the most funding by virtue of having more representatives securing earmarks, smaller states punch above their weight in the Senate — particularly when their delegations achieve exalted positions of seniority.

Hence Washington state — with Murray and Cantwell, the Commerce Committee ranking member, representing it — is way out in front.

By contrast, the second- and third-most populous states — Texas and Florida — received a grand total of zero earmarked funds, because their GOP senators didn't request any. California, with the largest population, is No. 16 in the ranks; New York is 12th.

Here are the top 10 states by earmarked funds procured in the Senate bills, clearly skewing toward smaller, typically reddish states:

The Transportation-HUD spending bill continues to be the go-to place for earmarks, accounting for 27 percent of all individual projects in the Senate bills and about one-third of all the earmarked dollars. The next-closest bill, Labor-HHS-Education, has half the earmarked amount that the "T-HUD" bill does.

Top agencies and programs with earmarked funds are housed within, that's right, the departments of Transportation and Housing and Urban Development, with HUD leading the pack thanks to its ever-popular Community Development Fund accounting for all of that department's earmarks.

Transportation isn't far behind, thanks largely to highway projects, followed by Health and Human Services and its Health Resources and Services Administration account, which funds community health centers. Defense Department military construction projects and the Army Corps of Engineers round out the group of $1 billion-plus agencies.

Here are the top accounts for earmarked funds in this year's crop of bills:

The biggest individual earmarks are largely within Army Corps accounts funded in the draft Energy-Water bill, with some military construction and transportation projects and two mega NIST-based university construction earmarks thrown in on behalf of Collins and McConnell.

#6000. It Takes a Family

The answers aren’t political and institutional; they are deeply relational.

John Mulaney in Saturday Night Live’s “Sister” sketch

The recent Saturday Night Live “Sister” skit hit a nerve with its fake ad for a 24-hour elder-care service. The service is “completely free,” provided you’re the brother.

“My dad means the world to me,” it begins, with comedian John Mulaney narrating. “So, when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible. I didn’t want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aide could cost thousands a week. I didn’t know where to turn.”

#5996. Rove’s Black Friday Deals Offer Up To 55% Transfer Bonuses—Plus 10x On Hotels That Earn Points And Perks

Rove is offering up to 55% more miles when you transfer to five airline and hotel programs, along with 10 miles per dollar on hotel bookings that still earn hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits. For the hotel offer there’s no stay deadline, so you can book future travel on Black Friday and collect the higher earning rate. Rove is a standalone rewards program. You earn its miles through travel bookings, shopping, dining and gift cards, then redeem them for travel or transfer them to airline and hotel programs. There’s no particular credit card you need to carry. Most of these offers last just one day. Here’s the schedule Rove gave me: November 26–30: transfer bonuses and double referral bonuses, ending at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Monday, November 30. Black Friday, November 27: the 10x Loyalty Eligible hotel offer, boosted shopping and gift card earnings, first hotel booking bonus and double qualifying miles. These end at 11:59 p.m. Eastern that night. 40%–55% Transfer Bonuses To Five Programs The same percentage bonus applies to Japan Airlines Mileage Bank, Air France KLM Flying Blue, Finnair Plus, Copa ConnectMiles and ALL Accor. Your Rove status determines the percentage. The four airlines normally transfer 1:1. Accor’s normal ratio is 1.5 Rove miles to 1 Accor point. Here’s what transferring 15,000 Rove miles gets you: Rove Status Bonus Airline Miles Or Avios Accor Points Member or Gold 40% 21,000 14,000 Platinum 50% 22,500 15,000 Diamond 55% 23,250 15,500 Those percentages already include the extra transfer bonus for Platinum and Diamond. Japan Airlines is worth looking at for its own flights and partner awards, including American Airlines and Alaska Airlines itineraries with three free stopovers. Rove offered everyone a 50% Japan Airlines transfer bonus in October, though. The 40% offer for most members is lower than that, while Diamond’s 55% is higher. Japan Airlines miles expire after 36 months, so a bonus doesn’t make them a good place to park miles indefinitely. Finnair is useful even if you don’t plan to fly Finnair. You can move Avios to British Airways at 1:1. Your Finnair account needs to be at least 30 days old before you can link it to another Avios program. Accor points are generally worth 2 euro cents each toward eligible hotel stays. The 15,000 Rove miles in the table therefore produce €280, €300 or €310 in hotel value, depending on status. Platinum effectively gets a 1:1 transfer to Accor during this promotion, and Diamond does slightly better. 10x Hotel Miles While Keeping Hotel Points And Benefits On November 27, new Loyalty Eligible hotel bookings earn 10 Rove miles per dollar. Rove says there are no property or rate exclusions within that category, and no promotional deadline to complete the stay. I’ve liked this feature since it launched. You can earn Rove miles while retaining hotel program points, qualifying nights and applicable elite benefits, along with the rewards from the card you use to pay. A $1,000 qualifying room subtotal earns 10,000 Rove miles. At 1.5 cents per mile, that’s $150 in additional travel value, before the hotel and credit card rewards. 5,000 Miles On A First Hotel Booking Has Different Rules Promo code BF500 adds 5,000 Rove miles to an eligible first Rove Rate hotel booking of $500 or more made on Black Friday. Join if you aren’t already a member and then take advantage of this. Rove clarified that you must never have booked a hotel through them before. Someone who’s already made a Loyalty Eligible reservation doesn’t qualify merely because this would be their first Rove Rate booking. An existing Rove account can qualify if it hasn’t booked a hotel. The code can combine with an eligible Rove elite hotel discount. However, Rove Rate bookings don’t earn hotel points or elite night credit, or guarantee hotel elite benefits. At exactly $500, the bonus adds 10 Rove miles per dollar to the booking’s standard earnings. I’ve covered a 5,000 mile first booking offer at the same spending threshold before. Double Qualifying Miles Includes Purchased Miles Boost Black Friday transactions that ordinarily earn qualifying miles will earn twice as many toward Rove status. Rove confirms that includes purchased Miles Boost and elevated earnings for elite members. For example, $1,000 in qualifying hotel spending at the promotional 10x rate generates 10,000 redeemable miles and 20,000 qualifying miles. The extra status credit doesn’t double the redeemable miles you can transfer or spend. Rove’s annual requirements remain: Gold: 50,000 qualifying miles and 5 qualifying transactions. Platinum: 125,000 qualifying miles and 10 qualifying transactions. Diamond: 250,000 qualifying miles and 20 qualifying transactions. Flat bonuses such as BF500’s 5,000 miles don’t ordinarily qualify, so they aren’t part of the doubling. Status earned for 2026 lasts through December 31, 2027. Travel counts toward the year it’s completed, while shopping and gift card purchases count by purchase date. A hotel stay ending in 2027 won’t be 2026 qualifying activity because it was booked in 2026. Higher Gift Card Earnings And The Full Shopping List Rove is offering up to 30% more miles on nearly all gift cards on Black Friday. A 30% increase would turn a 5x rate into 6.5x, for instance. (The actual rate depends on the gift card.) Rove sells gift cards marked for instant mileage earning which can help with this weekend’s transfer bonuses. #5995. Elon Musk Owes South Africa Nothing

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa (left) and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk

Last week, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa arrived in Silicon Valley seeking investment. He also had a message for Elon Musk: Remember your South African roots and “give back.”

It is an extraordinary appeal from the leader of a country crippled by unemployment, corruption, and economic stagnation. His African National Congress bears most of the responsibility. Yet Ramaphosa came to America, begging bowl in hand, asking successful entrepreneurs to help repair the damage. His government, meanwhile, obstructs one of the most obvious ways Musk could help — allowing Starlink to operate in South Africa.

Marian L. Tupy is the founder and editor of HumanProgress.org and a senior fellow at the Cato Institute’s Center for Global Liberty and Prosperity.

#5993. Cathay Pacific Asia Miles Announces Partner Award Devaluation, Starting January 5

Starting in January, it’ll take more Cathay Pacific miles to fly British Airways first class from Los Angeles to London than to fly Cathay first class all the way from New York to Hong Kong. The London flight goes from 135,000 to 162,000 Asia Miles each way. Hong Kong stays at 160,000. For two people booking London, that’s an extra 54,000 miles one way. A week after Chase added 1:1 transfers to Cathay Pacific, Cathay tells me its partner airlines are charging it more for award seats. It’s raising the mileage price of selected partner awards and dropping Companion Ticket Awards. The new rates kick in at midnight in Hong Kong on January 5, 2027. In the U.S., get your ticket issued before 11 a.m. Eastern on Monday, January 4 (10 a.m. Central, 8 a.m. in Los Angeles) for future travel to book at the old rates. Few things compare to seeing the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in person on a crisp November morning. Watching massive balloons float down the streets of New York City is an iconic holiday experience on many families’ travel wish lists. Unfortunately, due to severe weather in New York on Nov. 26, 2026, the parade has been postponed to Saturday, Nov. 28.

The last time weather grounded the parade was back in 1971. The parade will now start at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday.

Typically, seeing the parade requires forgoing (or delaying) a traditional Thanksgiving meal at home. However, it will likely be well worth the effort once you see your child giddy with excitement as their favorite cartoon characters float by to the tune of a marching band in full regalia, while giant floats with entertainers glide by at street level.

Note, though, that more than 3.5 million people attend the parade in person each year. It’s important to strategize your visit so you are not far from the curb, struggling to catch a glimpse of the street.

There are several things you’ll want to keep in mind as you plan your day at the parade. Here are our top tips for viewing the 100th annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in 2026.

If you want to get an up-close view of the balloons featured in the annual parade, you won’t want to miss the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Balloon Inflation. Inflation occurs the day before the parade, starting at 1 p.m. on the Upper West Side, at 72nd Street and Columbus Avenue, near the American Museum of Natural History. It runs until 6 p.m., so you have several hours to sneak a peek at what’s to come during the parade. (Tip: The line opens at noon.)

There are 32 balloons that will transform from flat to fully inflated during the course of the afternoon. There are some fun new floats to keep an eye out for this year. To name a few, Bob the Minion riding a giant banana, Sorcerer Mickey, the Geico gecko and Earl the Squirrel, a balloon based on a real-life squirrel who made his home in Universal Orlando's Christmas tree several years ago and has now become the park's official holiday mascot.

Inflating a giant balloon the height of a four-story building takes time. Long lines form as the balloons become fully inflated in the early evening, so you may want to test your luck by arriving closer to 3 p.m., when most of the balloons start taking shape.

To get to the event location via public transportation, allow extra time; the subway station at 72nd Street tends to get very crowded as the afternoon wears on. You can also hail a cab or use a ride-hailing service, though you’ll want to be dropped off a block or two north of the gated-off section to avoid delays. Once you're in the line, you'll progress north and can exit west along any block from West 82nd to West 86th streets.

TPG tip: The closest subway station to the entrance point is the B and C stop at 72nd Street and Central Park West. Consider taking the 1, 2 or 3 train to Broadway and 72nd Street instead. It’s a few blocks west but an easy walk — just follow the crowds.

Related: These are the best New York City hotels for families to check out

Some parade-goers arrive as early as 4 a.m. to snag a coveted front-row spot along the route.

Plan accordingly if you have a particular location in mind. For example, prime seats at covered bus stops start filling up around 4 a.m., while you might be able to get front-row curb seating closer to 6 a.m.

Should you have deeper pockets and want to avoid being outside in the elements, you can pay for a parade brunch with a view along the parade route. Just be sure to make these reservations well in advance, as they tend to fill up quickly. Or, of course, you could book a room with a view directly on the parade route.

For those arriving later in the morning, you can stand in the closed-off side streets leading to the parade. You might be 10-15 people back, but you can still see most of the action.

The parade starts at 8:30 a.m. at Central Park West on 77th Street. Since the route is 2.5 miles long, it can take close to an hour for the lead marchers to reach Macy's. This means you’ll have some idle time before you can start watching the spectacle.

Because you could find yourself waiting several hours for the parade to show up, you’ll want to bring some stuff to stay occupied, like snacks, drinks and games. A backup charger is also a good idea.

You can bring camping chairs, buckets or anything else you may want to sit on to the parade, though these items are not very helpful for the parade itself, since most people stand. Still, at the very least, you’ll probably want to have some hotel towels or blankets to sit on instead of the hard, cold, gum-covered New York City sidewalks.

Don’t forget proper attire, including jackets, hats, gloves and umbrellas if rain is in the forecast, since the weather can turn quickly in late fall.

Like at home, excitement builds as the parade start time nears, and before long, cheers erupt as the parade comes into view. However, what you may not realize from watching at home is how interactive the experience can be. You may get high-fives from clowns and even confetti in your hair.

Not everything you see on TV happens along the parade route, either. Some performances, including those by the Radio City Rockettes and various singing and dance groups, only occur in front of Macy’s Herald Square (where the cameras are). As a result, you’ll want to manage your expectations. Don’t worry about what you’re missing. Instead, focus on all that’s taking place in front of you: the floats, balloons and festivities.

Related: 10 tips for flying during the holidays

The parade covers so much of the city that there isn’t one best hotel for attending the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. While some hotels are physically on the parade route, it’s not as simple as booking a room at one of these properties and watching the festivities from your window.

Sure, some windows at the route-adjacent hotels offer good views — but hotels are savvy, so those rooms are often sold as part of pricier parade packages. As such, you’ll have to pay more and often meet minimum stay requirements to see the parade from your actual hotel room.

If you don’t want to splurge to see all the action from your room, ask if your hotel has a special viewing area for guests. Often, hotels on the parade route have some space outside where patrons can watch the parade as it passes.

A few properties on the parade route include:

Should you have trouble securing a room at a property on the parade route or wish to save a little money, consider staying a block or more off the route at properties like The St. Regis New York and Park Hyatt New York. Both are a very short walk to and from the parade.

Some more points-friendly hotels that are within walking distance of the parade route include:

Related: 10 festive hotels for people who really love the holidays

Since New York City is an incredible place to be for the holidays, there are all kinds of other ways to celebrate the season after kicking it off with the parade. Be sure to see Santa in person at Santaland on the eighth floor of Macy’s on 34th Street (reservations are required). The Big Apple Circus, under the big top in Lincoln Center, is a sure-fire family pleaser. Also, peruse some of the festive holiday markets throughout the city when you’re not busy ice skating at Rockefeller Center or catching a performance of a Christmas classic like “The Nutcracker” or “A Christmas Carol.”

#5991. DSA Is Right: Congressman-Elect Mocked For Refusing TSA Facial Scan—But He Brought A Passport Card, And The Photo Is Optional

The democratic socialist gets some of the explanation wrong. However, the people demanding his arrest appear to have a bigger problem with the rules than he does.

Rabb, a Pennsylvania state representative, was elected to represent Philadelphia in Congress and takes office in January.

In the video, he says he’s returning to Philadelphia from Boston. He says he doesn’t have a REAL ID card. He got a passport card so he wouldn’t need to carry his actual passport. He says TSA’s equipment wouldn’t process his identification, employees asked for another ID, and he didn’t have one with him. He also says he’d told them he didn’t consent to the photograph.

DSA Congressman Chris Rabb already working for the people by refusing to let TSA take his photo and also refusing to have an ID card. So brave. https://t.co/DnZSKeKZ7e

— Lee Kuan Yimby (@LeeKuanYimby) November 23, 2026

The State Department says a U.S. passport card can be used for domestic air travel instead of a REAL ID driver’s license. It fits in a wallet. It doesn’t work for international air travel, but Boston to Philadelphia isn’t international.

REAL ID enforcement doesn’t mean every passenger needs a state license with a star. A passport, passport card, and other documents on TSA’s accepted identification list are acceptable.

Rabb’s most useful advice is simple: Just say, “I don’t consent to being photographed.” That’s TSA’s published policy. Travelers can decline facial recognition and use the standard ID verification process instead. Rabb Wants To Avoid Being Put In A Database Rabb says he’s trying to avoid being put into another database. Too late! The standard checkpoint camera compares your face to the photograph on the ID you present. TSA says the image isn’t saved after a positive match, apart from limited testing used to evaluate the technology. You don’t necessarily have to believe them. Touchless programs can work differently. Identifying an enrolled traveler using a gallery of existing government photographs doesn’t add you to the database, you’re already there. Opting out doesn’t remove your travel records. The government already receives passenger information for Secure Flight screening. And obtaining a passport card already means you supplied a photograph. There are cameras everywhere, but for the most part there’s so much data that at least we benefit from security through obscurity. At least we did before AI made it all so much more easily searchable. I’ve covered passenger information collected for aviation security being used to help immigration agents intercept travelers. Law enforcement has access to passenger data even without this additional photo. Positive ID Matches Don’t Contribute Much To Security Positive identification is supposed to make sure you can’t simply fly under somebody else’s name. That’s necessary for the government’s database of people they want to bar from flying or ensure receiving extra screenig works. Of course, the database itself is corrupted. The terrorist screening database has over two million people in it. I’ve written about the sprawling watchlist system and agents using the no fly list to retaliate against people who wouldn’t become informants. Identity checks also serve a separate economic purpose for airlines. Matching the traveler to the name on a nontransferable ticket helps enforce price discrimination. If you could buy a cheap ticket months ahead and freely sell it to someone traveling tomorrow, you’d compete with the airline’s expensive last-minute fare. Preventing that resale helps airlines separate passengers willing to plan ahead from those willing to pay more. It doesn’t create a real aviation security benefit. I Made My Own Compromise Long Ago I’m an old line civil libertarian on this. I was late signing up for Global Entry in 2013 because I didn’t like volunteering fingerprints and a photograph to the government in exchange for easier travel. When I finally joined, before the Edward Snowden revelations, I was already writing about government collection of cellphone geolocation data, license plate readers, and other surveillance. The government already had the information, so I might as well get the benefits. At the same time, I think we’ve largely lost this argument in practice. I’ve written about the spread of checkpoint photography and biometric boarding gates becoming normal. The surveillance state has won. Rabb himself concedes that his refusal won’t make much practical difference. He sees value in reminding people they can object and in resisting normalization. I have sympathy for this. What To Do If You Want To Opt Out Bring an accepted physical ID and make the request before the camera takes your picture. “I’m opting out of the facial photograph. Please use the standard ID check.” Hand over the document and cooperate with that check. Separate a camera objection from a document problem. If the reader won’t process a passport card, ask for a supervisor and an alternative document check. Carrying a second accepted ID can save time if something fails. With millions of passengers processed per day small failure rates mean actual failures happen regularly. Escalate a refusal of the opt out calmly. TSA says you can request a supervisor or passenger support specialist. Record the airport, checkpoint, date, time, and what was said, and submit a complaint. They’ll go ahead and ignore or dismiss it. Don’t confuse any of this with arriving without allowable identification. Since February, TSA’s ConfirmID requirement costs $45. The payment covers a ten day travel period and doesn’t guarantee identity verification. Meanwhile, at the border, U.S. citizens can request an alternative inspection. Noncitizens, including permanent residents, generally cannot claim the same photo opt-out. Rabb will shortly have a better tool than an argument at a document podium: a seat in Congress. Separate a camera objection from a document problem. If the reader won’t process a passport card, ask for a supervisor and an alternative document check. Carrying a second accepted ID can save time if something fails. With millions of passengers processed per day small failure rates mean actual failures happen regularly.

Escalate a refusal of the opt out calmly. TSA says you can request a supervisor or passenger support specialist. Record the airport, checkpoint, date, time, and what was said, and submit a complaint. They’ll go ahead and ignore or dismiss it.

Don’t confuse any of this with arriving without allowable identification. Since February, TSA’s ConfirmID requirement costs $45. The payment covers a ten day travel period and doesn’t guarantee identity verification.

Meanwhile, at the border, U.S. citizens can request an alternative inspection. Noncitizens, including permanent residents, generally cannot claim the same photo opt-out.

Rabb will shortly have a better tool than an argument at a document podium: a seat in Congress. #5990. How Long Can Jensen Huang and Nvidia Defy Gravity?

His reinstatement at Trump’s urging is a perilous high-wire act.

Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks at the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nev., January 6, 2026.

It’s foolish to be astonished by anything anymore. Still, Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer, just eleven days after his resignation and six days after the board of directors said it had no intention to reinstate him, is surprising, to say the least.

The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia’s statement that the board had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” and is “confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

#5988. Thieves Are Stealing Used Cooking Oil From Hotels—It May Be Fueling Your Next Flight

Thieves stole 350 gallons of cooking oil from an airport hotel in Pennsylvania. The haul was valued at $2,100, and the victim named by state police was a biofuel company. Hotel kitchen grease has become valuable enough to steal. Used grease can fetch more than new! And it can eventually wind up fueling an airline flight and helping a carrier meet its environmental goals. Pennsylvania State Police responded on November 18 to the theft at 3400 Airport Road, the Days Hotel by Wyndham Allentown Airport / Lehigh Valley. The hotel has a restaurant and banquet facilities, so there’s a kitchen generating oil to collect. The loss works out to $6 per gallon. The listed victim was Buffalo Biodiesel, which deals in used cooking oil, which it processes and sends to biodiesel refineries. People steal astonishing things from hotels. I’ve covered mattresses, a lobby grand piano, and even a fireplace being taken. Two men carried an entire ATM out of a Country Inn & Suites. Used fryer oil seems much less attractive? But there’s a ready buyer for it, and hotels have been caught up in a much broader rash of cooking oil thefts: Hilton Short Hills, New Jersey: Police caught two men taking cooking oil around 3 a.m.. They’d arrived in a white Penske truck and were charged with theft and conspiracy. Brick Hotel, Pennsylvania: An attempted theft caused a used oil spill that required an environmental cleanup and closed a municipal parking lot. A hotel in Largs, Scotland: Two men arrived in a van around 1 a.m. and carried away cooking oil in blue buckets in order to convert it into biodiesel for profit. Old Ground Hotel, Ireland: Two men who pleaded guilty to stealing used cooking oil said they wanted it to fuel their cars. In September, two defendants pleaded guilty in a federal case involving 19 people charged over a cooking oil theft operation spanning ten states. Trucks were taking the oil from restaurant collection tanks, warehouses consolidated it, the oil was sold across states and the effort was implicated in money laundering. The North American Renderers Association estimates annual used cooking oil theft at $300 million to $500 million. Once a hotel is done frying food, the oil can be collected and sold for processing into fuel. Buffalo Biodiesel supplies collection containers, picks up the oil, and processes it at its Tonawanda, New York facility before shipping it to refineries. These are the company’s processing tanks: Used cooking oil gets processed into sustainable aviation fuel. Refineries turn the fats and oils into fuel that can be blended with conventional jet fuel. Airlines want that fuel to meet environmental targets, and government subsidies prop up that market. This can create some very strange incentives. I’ve written about the arbitrage that makes used cooking oil more valuable than new oil in Malaysia. The government subsidizes cooking oil for food. Meanwhile, the biofuel market pays for oil classified as waste. In July 2025, subsidized fresh oil sold for 2.50 ringgit per kilogram while collectors could pay up to 3.50 ringgit for used oil. That’s a 40% spread. This turns into a greenwashing scam that actually creates more problems than it solves. By paying for “used” oil restaurants are encouraged to ‘create’ used oil, replacing their oil sooner. When you pay more than fresh oil costs, the incentive actually becomes skipping the cooking part altogether. But the environmental case depends on making use of waste that already exists. Instead, diverting fresh palm oil into that market increases the demand for new cooling oil production (and the pressure to clear land for it). The Simpsons got to this in 1998. In “Lard of the Dance,” Homer discovers that used grease has resale value: “Used grease is worth money? Then my arteries are clogged with yellow gold!” He and Bart eventually try stealing the school’s grease. Groundskeeper Willie catches them — he’s been saving it for retirement. New Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® cardholders can earn 50% bonus points on purchases in categories that normally earn 1x (up to 20,000 bonus points), and Aeroplan members get 10,000 points off hotel redemptions and 15,000 off car rentals when redeeming 50,000 points or more (codes "BFHOTEL26" and "BFAUTO26," through Nov. 30).

You can also expect some special offers for American Airlines AAdvantage members, so be sure to check back on Friday.

You can also expect some great points deals using Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points.
